question.worked_solution:
First, we write $1\,\frac{1}{3}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
1\,\frac{1}{3}=\frac{(1\times 3)+1}{3}=\frac{4}{3}
$$

We also write  $2\,\frac{1}{4}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
2\,\frac{1}{4}=\frac{(2\times 4)+1}{4}=\frac{9}{4}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}\times \frac{9}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}\times \frac{9}{4} & =\frac{4}{4}\times \frac{9}{3} \\  & =1\times 3 \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
1\,\frac{1}{3}\times 2\,\frac{1}{4}=3
$$
